note: Hand-written for the site (explanations and examples are our own), graded like Taiwan's senior high English (owner, 2026-11-06). An example's or question's en is the English sentence itself (the English UI shows no hint). Edit this file, then run: python tools/build_grammar.py

form.zh: had ＋ 過去分詞（所有人稱都一樣）
form.en: had + past participle (the same for every subject)

explain.zh: 說「過去某個時間點之前已經發生」的事：When I got to the station, the train had already left.（我到車站時，火車已經開走了。）先發生的用過去完成式，後發生的用過去式。
explain.en: For something that happened before another past moment: When I got to the station, the train had already left. The earlier event takes the past perfect, the later one the past simple.

notes.zh: 有 before、after 讓順序很清楚時，也可以兩個都用過去式。
notes.en: With before or after making the order clear, the past simple is also fine for both.

mistakes.wrong: I had visited Tokyo last year.
mistakes.right: I visited Tokyo last year.
mistakes.zh: 只有一件過去的事、沒有更早的參考點，用過去式就好。
mistakes.en: With just one past event and no earlier reference point, use the past simple.

mistakes.wrong: She told me she has lost her key.
mistakes.right: She told me she had lost her key.
mistakes.zh: 比「告訴我」更早發生，用 had lost。
mistakes.en: It happened before she told me: had lost.

examples.text: By the time we arrived, the movie had started.
examples.zh: 我們到的時候電影已經開始了。
examples.en: By the time we arrived, the movie had started.

examples.text: I had never seen snow before I went to Hokkaido.
examples.zh: 去北海道之前我從來沒看過雪。
examples.en: I had never seen snow before I went to Hokkaido.

examples.text: He was tired because he had worked all night.
examples.zh: 他很累，因為他工作了一整晚。
examples.en: He was tired because he had worked all night.

quiz.q: When the police arrived, the thief（　）.
quiz.zh: 警察到的時候，小偷已經逃走了。
quiz.en: When the police arrived, the thief had escaped.

quiz.q: She（　）the book before she saw the film.
quiz.zh: 她看電影之前已經讀過那本書了。
quiz.en: She had read the book before she saw the film.

quiz.q: I realized I（　）my wallet at home.
quiz.zh: 我發現我把錢包忘在家裡了。
quiz.en: I realized I had left my wallet at home.

form.zh: have／has been ＋ V-ing　常和 for、since、all day 一起用
form.en: have / has been + verb-ing · often with for, since, all day

explain.zh: 強調一個動作從過去一直持續到現在（而且可能還在進行）：I have been studying for three hours.（我已經讀了三個小時的書。）It has been raining since this morning.
explain.en: For an activity that started in the past and is still going on (or has just stopped): I have been studying for three hours. It has been raining since this morning.

notes.zh: 強調「持續多久」用完成進行式，強調「完成了多少」用完成式：I've been writing emails all morning. ／ I've written ten emails.
notes.en: Stress the duration with the continuous, the result with the simple: I've been writing emails all morning / I've written ten emails.

notes.zh: 狀態動詞（know、like、own）不用進行式：I've known her for years.
notes.en: State verbs aren't continuous: I've known her for years.

mistakes.wrong: I am waiting here for an hour.
mistakes.right: I have been waiting here for an hour.
mistakes.zh: 持續到現在的一段時間要用完成進行式。
mistakes.en: A duration up to now needs the perfect continuous.

mistakes.wrong: She has been knowing him since 2019.
mistakes.right: She has known him since 2019.
mistakes.zh: know 是狀態動詞，不用進行式。
mistakes.en: know is a state verb.

examples.text: How long have you been learning English?
examples.zh: 你學英文多久了？
examples.en: How long have you been learning English?

examples.text: My legs hurt. I've been walking all day.
examples.zh: 我腿好痠，走了一整天。
examples.en: My legs hurt. I've been walking all day.

examples.text: They have been living in Taichung since 2015.
examples.zh: 他們從 2015 年起就住在台中。
examples.en: They have been living in Taichung since 2015.

quiz.q: We（　）for the bus for twenty minutes.
quiz.zh: 我們已經等公車等了二十分鐘。
quiz.en: We have been waiting for the bus for twenty minutes.

quiz.q: Your eyes are red. Have you（　）?
quiz.zh: 你眼睛好紅，你一直在哭嗎？
quiz.en: Your eyes are red. Have you been crying?

quiz.q: He has（　）the guitar since he was ten.
quiz.zh: 他從十歲開始就在彈吉他。
quiz.en: He has been playing the guitar since he was ten.

title.zh: 未來進行式和未來完成式

form.zh: will be ＋ V-ing（到時候正在…）・will have ＋ 過去分詞（到時候已經…）
form.en: will be + verb-ing (will be doing) · will have + past participle (will have done)

explain.zh: 未來進行式說未來某個時間點「正在做」：This time tomorrow, I'll be flying to Tokyo. 未來完成式說到某個時間點時「已經完成」：By next June, I will have graduated.（到明年六月我就畢業了。）
explain.en: The future continuous is what will be in progress at a future time: This time tomorrow, I'll be flying to Tokyo. The future perfect is what will be finished by then: By next June, I will have graduated.

notes.zh: 未來完成式常和 by ＋ 時間一起用：by Friday、by the end of the year。
notes.en: The future perfect goes with by + time: by Friday, by the end of the year.

mistakes.wrong: By 2030, I will finish my degree.
mistakes.right: By 2030, I will have finished my degree.
mistakes.zh: by 某時「已經完成」用未來完成式。
mistakes.en: “Done by” a time takes the future perfect.

mistakes.wrong: At 8 p.m. tonight I will watch the game, so don't call.
mistakes.right: At 8 p.m. tonight I will be watching the game, so don't call.
mistakes.zh: 那個時間點「正在」做，用未來進行式。
mistakes.en: In progress at that time: future continuous.

examples.text: Don't call me at nine. I'll be having dinner.
examples.zh: 九點別打給我，我會在吃晚餐。
examples.en: Don't call me at nine. I'll be having dinner.

examples.text: By the time you get here, we will have eaten.
examples.zh: 等你到的時候，我們已經吃完了。
examples.en: By the time you get here, we will have eaten.

examples.text: Next year, they will have been married for twenty years.
examples.zh: 明年他們就結婚滿二十年了。
examples.en: Next year, they will have been married for twenty years.

quiz.q: By the end of this month, I（　）this book.
quiz.zh: 到這個月底，我就會讀完這本書。
quiz.en: By the end of this month, I will have finished this book.

quiz.q: This time next week, we（　）on the beach in Kenting.
quiz.zh: 下週的這個時候，我們會正躺在墾丁的海灘上。
quiz.en: This time next week, we will be lying on the beach in Kenting.

quiz.q: The store will（　）by the time we get there.
quiz.zh: 等我們到的時候，店已經關了。
quiz.en: The store will have closed by the time we get there.

form.zh: 進行：is／are being ＋ p.p.・完成：has／have been ＋ p.p.・助動詞：can／must／should be ＋ p.p.
form.en: continuous: is / are being + p.p. · perfect: has / have been + p.p. · modal: can / must / should be + p.p.

explain.zh: 被動語態可以用在各種時態：The road is being repaired.（路正在整修。）The tickets have been sold out.（票已經賣完了。）This medicine must be taken after meals.（這個藥必須飯後吃。）
explain.en: The passive works in every tense: The road is being repaired, The tickets have been sold out, This medicine must be taken after meals.

notes.zh: 助動詞後面一定是 be ＋ p.p.，be 不變：should be done、can be seen。
notes.en: After a modal it's always be + p.p.: should be done, can be seen.

mistakes.wrong: The house is building now.
mistakes.right: The house is being built now.
mistakes.zh: 房子是「被蓋」，進行式被動是 is being built。
mistakes.en: The house is being built — continuous passive.

mistakes.wrong: The work must finished today.
mistakes.right: The work must be finished today.
mistakes.zh: 助動詞被動要有 be。
mistakes.en: A modal passive needs be.

examples.text: My phone is being repaired, so I can't call you.
examples.zh: 我的手機在送修，所以沒辦法打給你。
examples.en: My phone is being repaired, so I can't call you.

examples.text: Has the package been delivered yet?
examples.zh: 包裹送到了嗎？
examples.en: Has the package been delivered yet?

examples.text: Plastic bottles should be recycled.
examples.zh: 塑膠瓶應該回收。
examples.en: Plastic bottles should be recycled.

quiz.q: The meeting room（　）right now.
quiz.zh: 會議室現在正在打掃。
quiz.en: The meeting room is being cleaned right now.

quiz.q: All the cookies have（　）.
quiz.zh: 餅乾全被吃光了。
quiz.en: All the cookies have been eaten.

quiz.q: Phones must（　）off during the exam.
quiz.zh: 考試期間手機必須關機。
quiz.en: Phones must be turned off during the exam.

title.zh: 與現在事實相反的假設
title.en: Unreal present: If I were …, I would …

form.zh: If ＋ 主詞 ＋ 過去式（be 一律 were）, 主詞 ＋ would／could／might ＋ 原形
form.en: If + subject + past simple (be → were), subject + would / could / might + verb

explain.zh: 說「現在不是這樣，如果是的話會…」：If I had more time, I would learn to swim.（如果我有更多時間，就會去學游泳。）實際上我沒有時間。be 動詞不分人稱都用 were：If I were you, I'd apologize.
explain.en: For situations that aren't true now: If I had more time, I would learn to swim (but I don't). be is were for every subject: If I were you, I'd apologize.

notes.zh: 跟「真的可能發生」的條件不同：If it rains, I'll stay home.（有可能下雨）
notes.en: Compare a real possibility: If it rains, I'll stay home.

mistakes.wrong: If I am rich, I would buy a house.
mistakes.right: If I were rich, I would buy a house.
mistakes.zh: 與現在事實相反，if 子句用過去式 were。
mistakes.en: Unreal present: were in the if clause.

mistakes.wrong: If I knew the answer, I will tell you.
mistakes.right: If I knew the answer, I would tell you.
mistakes.zh: 主要子句用 would，不用 will。
mistakes.en: The main clause takes would, not will.

examples.text: If I lived closer to school, I wouldn't have to get up so early.
examples.zh: 如果我住得離學校近一點，就不用這麼早起了。
examples.en: If I lived closer to school, I wouldn't have to get up so early.

examples.text: What would you do if you won the lottery?
examples.zh: 如果你中了樂透，你會做什麼？
examples.en: What would you do if you won the lottery?

examples.text: If I were you, I would take the job.
examples.zh: 如果我是你，我會接下那份工作。
examples.en: If I were you, I would take the job.

quiz.q: If I（　）a bird, I would fly around the world.
quiz.zh: 如果我是一隻鳥，我會飛遍全世界。
quiz.en: If I were a bird, I would fly around the world.

quiz.q: If she had a car, she（　）drive to work.
quiz.zh: 如果她有車，她就會開車上班。
quiz.en: If she had a car, she would drive to work.

quiz.q: I would call him if I（　）his number.
quiz.zh: 如果我知道他的號碼，我就會打給他。
quiz.en: I would call him if I knew his number.

points.pattern: If I had …, I would have …

title.zh: 與過去事實相反的假設
title.en: Unreal past: If I had …, I would have …

form.zh: If ＋ 主詞 ＋ had ＋ p.p., 主詞 ＋ would／could／might have ＋ p.p.
form.en: If + subject + had + p.p., subject + would / could / might have + p.p.

explain.zh: 說「過去沒有發生，如果當時…就會…」：If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.（如果我當時更用功，就會通過考試了。）實際上沒有用功，也沒通過。
explain.en: For things that didn't happen in the past: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam (but I didn't, and I didn't pass).

notes.zh: 口語常縮寫：I'd have known、If I'd known。
notes.en: Spoken short forms: I'd have known, If I'd known.

mistakes.wrong: If I knew you were coming, I would have cooked.
mistakes.right: If I had known you were coming, I would have cooked.
mistakes.zh: 過去的假設，if 子句用 had ＋ p.p.。
mistakes.en: Unreal past: had + p.p. in the if clause.

mistakes.wrong: If you had told me, I would help you.
mistakes.right: If you had told me, I would have helped you.
mistakes.zh: 主要子句用 would have ＋ p.p.。
mistakes.en: The main clause takes would have + p.p.

examples.text: If we had left earlier, we wouldn't have missed the train.
examples.zh: 如果我們早點出門，就不會錯過火車了。
examples.en: If we had left earlier, we wouldn't have missed the train.

examples.text: She could have won if she hadn't fallen.
examples.zh: 如果她沒有跌倒，就可能贏了。
examples.en: She could have won if she hadn't fallen.

examples.text: If I had known it was your birthday, I would have bought a gift.
examples.zh: 如果我知道那天是你生日，就會買禮物了。
examples.en: If I had known it was your birthday, I would have bought a gift.

quiz.q: If he（　）the alarm, he wouldn't have been late.
quiz.zh: 如果他有聽到鬧鐘，就不會遲到了。
quiz.en: If he had heard the alarm, he wouldn't have been late.

quiz.q: If you had asked me, I（　）you.
quiz.zh: 如果你當時問我，我就會幫你了。
quiz.en: If you had asked me, I would have helped you.

quiz.q: We would have gone to the beach if it（　）.
quiz.zh: 如果那天沒下雨，我們就會去海邊了。
quiz.en: We would have gone to the beach if it hadn't rained.

form.zh: 對現在：wish ＋ 過去式（were）・對過去：wish ＋ had ＋ p.p.・對未來或希望別人改變：wish ＋ would ＋ 原形
form.en: present: wish + past (were) · past: wish + had + p.p. · wanting change: wish + would + verb

explain.zh: wish 表示「但願（但事實不是）」，時態要往過去退一步：I wish I were taller.（真希望我高一點。）I wish I had listened to you.（真希望我當時有聽你的。）If only 意思一樣，語氣更強。
explain.en: wish means you'd like things to be different, so the tense moves back: I wish I were taller, I wish I had listened to you. If only means the same, more strongly.

notes.zh: 對可能實現的希望用 hope：I hope you feel better soon.（不用 wish）
notes.en: For real possibilities use hope: I hope you feel better soon.

mistakes.wrong: I wish I can speak French.
mistakes.right: I wish I could speak French.
mistakes.zh: wish 後面時態往過去退：could。
mistakes.en: After wish, move back a tense: could.

mistakes.wrong: I wish you pass the exam.
mistakes.right: I hope you pass the exam.
mistakes.zh: 有可能實現的希望用 hope。
mistakes.en: A real hope takes hope.

examples.text: I wish I didn't have to work today.
examples.zh: 真希望我今天不用上班。
examples.en: I wish I didn't have to work today.

examples.text: If only I had brought an umbrella!
examples.zh: 早知道就帶傘了！
examples.en: If only I had brought an umbrella!

examples.text: I wish my neighbors would stop making noise.
examples.zh: 真希望鄰居不要再吵了。
examples.en: I wish my neighbors would stop making noise.

quiz.q: I wish I（　）more free time.
quiz.zh: 真希望我有更多空閒時間。
quiz.en: I wish I had more free time.

quiz.q: I wish I（　）that cake. Now I feel sick.
quiz.zh: 真後悔吃了那塊蛋糕，現在不舒服。
quiz.en: I wish I hadn't eaten that cake. Now I feel sick.

quiz.q: I（　）you have a great trip!
quiz.zh: 祝你旅途愉快！
quiz.en: I hope you have a great trip!

form.zh: as if ＋ 過去式（好像…，但其實不是）・would rather ＋ 原形（寧願）・would rather ＋ 主詞 ＋ 過去式（希望別人…）
form.en: as if + past (as though — but not really) · would rather + verb (prefer) · would rather + subject + past (prefer someone else to)

explain.zh: as if 說「好像…一樣」，不是事實時用過去式：He talks as if he were the boss.（他說話的樣子好像他是老闆。）would rather 是「寧願」：I'd rather stay home tonight.
explain.en: as if means “as though”; for something untrue use the past: He talks as if he were the boss. would rather means “prefer”: I'd rather stay home tonight.

notes.zh: 比較用 than：I'd rather walk than take the bus.
notes.en: Compare with than: I'd rather walk than take the bus.

mistakes.wrong: I would rather to stay here.
mistakes.right: I would rather stay here.
mistakes.zh: would rather 後面接原形，不加 to。
mistakes.en: would rather takes the bare verb.

mistakes.wrong: She acts as if she is a queen.
mistakes.right: She acts as if she were a queen.
mistakes.zh: 不是事實時，as if 後面用 were。
mistakes.en: For something untrue, use were after as if.

examples.text: He looked at me as if I were crazy.
examples.zh: 他看我的樣子好像我瘋了一樣。
examples.en: He looked at me as if I were crazy.

examples.text: I'd rather have tea than coffee.
examples.zh: 我寧願喝茶，不喝咖啡。
examples.en: I'd rather have tea than coffee.

examples.text: I'd rather you didn't tell anyone.
examples.zh: 我希望你不要告訴任何人。
examples.en: I'd rather you didn't tell anyone.

quiz.q: I'd rather（　）at home than go out tonight.
quiz.zh: 今晚我寧願待在家也不想出門。
quiz.en: I'd rather stay at home than go out tonight.

quiz.q: She talks as if she（　）everything.
quiz.zh: 她說話的樣子好像什麼都懂。
quiz.en: She talks as if she knew everything.

quiz.q: I'd rather you（　）smoke in the car.
quiz.zh: 我希望你不要在車裡抽菸。
quiz.en: I'd rather you didn't smoke in the car.

title.zh: 關係代名詞 whose、whom、介系詞 ＋ which
title.en: Relative pronouns: whose, whom, preposition + which

form.zh: whose ＋ 名詞（…的）・whom（受格的人）・介系詞 ＋ which／whom（the house in which …）
form.en: whose + noun (possessive) · whom (person as object) · preposition + which / whom (the house in which …)

explain.zh: whose 表示所有：I have a friend whose father is a pilot.（我有個朋友的爸爸是機師。）whom 是受格的人（正式）：the man whom I met。介系詞可以放在 which／whom 前面：the city in which I was born。
explain.en: whose shows possession: I have a friend whose father is a pilot. whom is a person as object (formal): the man whom I met. A preposition can go before which / whom: the city in which I was born.

notes.zh: 介系詞放前面時不能用 that 或 who：in which，不說 in that。
notes.en: After a preposition you can't use that or who: in which, not in that.

mistakes.wrong: The girl who her bike was stolen called the police.
mistakes.right: The girl whose bike was stolen called the police.
mistakes.zh: 「她的腳踏車」用 whose。
mistakes.en: “Her bike” is whose bike.

mistakes.wrong: This is the room in that I study.
mistakes.right: This is the room in which I study.
mistakes.zh: 介系詞後面用 which。
mistakes.en: After a preposition use which.

examples.text: That's the singer whose song went viral.
examples.zh: 那就是歌曲爆紅的那位歌手。
examples.en: That's the singer whose song went viral.

examples.text: The person to whom I spoke was very helpful.
examples.zh: 跟我說話的那個人很熱心。
examples.en: The person to whom I spoke was very helpful.

examples.text: This is the house in which my grandfather grew up.
examples.zh: 這是我爺爺從小長大的房子。
examples.en: This is the house in which my grandfather grew up.

quiz.q: I met a woman（　）son goes to my school.
quiz.zh: 我遇見一位女士，她兒子跟我同校。
quiz.en: I met a woman whose son goes to my school.

quiz.q: The chair on（　）you are sitting is very old.
quiz.zh: 你坐的那張椅子很老舊。
quiz.en: The chair on which you are sitting is very old.

quiz.q: He is the teacher from（　）I learned the most.
quiz.zh: 他是讓我學到最多的老師。
quiz.en: He is the teacher from whom I learned the most.

form.zh: 名詞, who／which ＋ 補充說明, …（前後加逗號，不能用 that）・, which 也可以指整句話
form.en: noun, who / which + extra information, … (commas; no that) · , which can refer to a whole clause

explain.zh: 加逗號的關係子句只是補充說明，拿掉也不影響句意：My sister, who lives in Taipei, is a nurse.（我姊姊住在台北，她是護理師。）, which 也能指前面整句：He passed the exam, which surprised everyone.
explain.en: With commas, the clause just adds information and could be dropped: My sister, who lives in Taipei, is a nurse. , which can refer to the whole idea: He passed the exam, which surprised everyone.

notes.zh: 非限定子句不能用 that，也不能省略關係代名詞。
notes.en: Non-defining clauses can't use that or drop the pronoun.

mistakes.wrong: Taipei 101, that was finished in 2004, is very tall.
mistakes.right: Taipei 101, which was finished in 2004, is very tall.
mistakes.zh: 逗號後面不能用 that。
mistakes.en: No that after a comma.

mistakes.wrong: She lost her phone, what made her upset.
mistakes.right: She lost her phone, which made her upset.
mistakes.zh: 指前面整件事用 , which。
mistakes.en: Referring to the whole clause: , which.

examples.text: Jiufen, which is near Keelung, is popular with tourists.
examples.zh: 九份靠近基隆，很受觀光客歡迎。
examples.en: Jiufen, which is near Keelung, is popular with tourists.

examples.text: My grandmother, who is 90, still walks every day.
examples.zh: 我奶奶九十歲了，還是每天散步。
examples.en: My grandmother, who is 90, still walks every day.

examples.text: The train was late, which meant we missed the show.
examples.zh: 火車誤點，結果我們錯過了表演。
examples.en: The train was late, which meant we missed the show.

quiz.q: Mr. Wang, （　）teaches history, is retiring this year.
quiz.zh: 王老師教歷史，今年要退休了。
quiz.en: Mr. Wang, who teaches history, is retiring this year.

quiz.q: It rained all weekend, （　）was disappointing.
quiz.zh: 整個週末都在下雨，真令人失望。
quiz.en: It rained all weekend, which was disappointing.

quiz.q: My phone, （　）I bought last month, has stopped working.
quiz.zh: 我的手機上個月才買，已經壞了。
quiz.en: My phone, which I bought last month, has stopped working.

form.zh: 地方 ＋ where ＋ 子句・時間 ＋ when ＋ 子句・the reason ＋ why ＋ 子句
form.en: place + where + clause · time + when + clause · the reason + why + clause

explain.zh: 說明地方、時間、原因時用關係副詞：This is the restaurant where we first met.（這是我們第一次見面的餐廳。）I'll never forget the day when I got my results. That's the reason why I quit.
explain.en: Use relative adverbs for places, times and reasons: This is the restaurant where we first met. I'll never forget the day when I got my results. That's the reason why I quit.

notes.zh: where ＝ in／at which，when ＝ on／in which。
notes.en: where = in / at which; when = on / in which.

notes.zh: 子句缺受詞時用 which／that，不用 where：the city (that) I visited。
notes.en: If the clause lacks an object, use which / that, not where: the city (that) I visited.

mistakes.wrong: This is the park where I like.
mistakes.right: This is the park (that) I like.
mistakes.zh: like 缺受詞，要用 that／which。
mistakes.en: like needs an object: use that / which.

mistakes.wrong: I remember the year which we moved here.
mistakes.right: I remember the year when we moved here.
mistakes.zh: 子句完整、說時間，用 when。
mistakes.en: The clause is complete and it's a time: when.

examples.text: Tainan is the city where I was born.
examples.zh: 台南是我出生的城市。
examples.en: Tainan is the city where I was born.

examples.text: Summer is the season when we go camping.
examples.zh: 夏天是我們去露營的季節。
examples.en: Summer is the season when we go camping.

examples.text: Nobody knows the reason why he left.
examples.zh: 沒有人知道他離開的原因。
examples.en: Nobody knows the reason why he left.

quiz.q: This is the hospital（　）my mother works.
quiz.zh: 這是我媽媽工作的醫院。
quiz.en: This is the hospital where my mother works.

quiz.q: Do you remember the day（　）we first met?
quiz.zh: 你記得我們第一次見面的那天嗎？
quiz.en: Do you remember the day when we first met?

quiz.q: Kyoto is a city（　）I have always wanted to visit.
quiz.zh: 京都是我一直想去的城市。
quiz.en: Kyoto is a city that I have always wanted to visit.

form.zh: whatever（任何…的東西／不論什麼）・whoever（任何…的人／不論誰）・wherever（不論哪裡）・whenever（不論何時）・however ＋ 形容詞（不論多…）
form.en: whatever · whoever · wherever · whenever · however + adjective (no matter how)

explain.zh: 這些字可以當「任何…的」：Take whatever you want.（你想拿什麼就拿。）也可以表示讓步「不論…」：Whatever happens, I'll support you.（不管發生什麼，我都支持你。）＝ No matter what happens …
explain.en: They mean “anything that”: Take whatever you want. They also mean “no matter”: Whatever happens, I'll support you (= No matter what happens …).

notes.zh: however 後面接形容詞或副詞：However hard it is, don't give up.
notes.en: however takes an adjective or adverb: However hard it is, don't give up.

mistakes.wrong: You can invite whomever wants to come.
mistakes.right: You can invite whoever wants to come.
mistakes.zh: 子句裡當主詞（wants 的主詞）用 whoever。
mistakes.en: It's the subject of wants: whoever.

mistakes.wrong: No matter how it is hard, keep going.
mistakes.right: No matter how hard it is, keep going.
mistakes.zh: how 後面緊接形容詞。
mistakes.en: how is followed directly by the adjective.

examples.text: You can sit wherever you like.
examples.zh: 你想坐哪裡都可以。
examples.en: You can sit wherever you like.

examples.text: Whoever finishes first gets a prize.
examples.zh: 最先完成的人有獎品。
examples.en: Whoever finishes first gets a prize.

examples.text: Call me whenever you need help.
examples.zh: 需要幫忙時隨時打給我。
examples.en: Call me whenever you need help.

quiz.q: （　）you do, don't tell Mom.
quiz.zh: 不管你做什麼，都別跟媽媽說。
quiz.en: Whatever you do, don't tell Mom.

quiz.q: （　）tired I am, I always cook dinner.
quiz.zh: 不論多累，我都會煮晚餐。
quiz.en: However tired I am, I always cook dinner.

quiz.q: Give the ticket to（　）needs it most.
quiz.zh: 把票給最需要的人。
quiz.en: Give the ticket to whoever needs it most.

form.zh: 主動：V-ing …, 主句（Walking home, I met Amy.）・被動：p.p. …, 主句（Written in 1900, the book …）・先發生：Having ＋ p.p. …,
form.en: active: V-ing …, main clause · passive: p.p. …, main clause · earlier action: Having + p.p. …,

explain.zh: 兩個子句主詞相同時，可以把一個子句縮成分詞：When I walked home, I met Amy. → Walking home, I met Amy. 主詞「被」做用過去分詞：Built in 1920, the station is a historic site.
explain.en: When both clauses share a subject, one can become a participle: When I walked home, I met Amy → Walking home, I met Amy. If the subject is acted on, use the past participle: Built in 1920, the station is a historic site.

notes.zh: 分詞的主詞必須跟主句主詞一樣，不然會變成「懸垂分詞」的錯誤。
notes.en: The participle's subject must be the main clause's subject, or it “dangles”.

mistakes.wrong: Walking into the room, the lights went off.
mistakes.right: Walking into the room, I saw the lights go off.
mistakes.zh: 走進房間的是「我」，不是燈。
mistakes.en: I walked in, not the lights.

mistakes.wrong: Writing in simple English, the book is easy to read.
mistakes.right: Written in simple English, the book is easy to read.
mistakes.zh: 書是「被寫」，用過去分詞。
mistakes.en: The book was written: past participle.

examples.text: Feeling tired, she went to bed early.
examples.zh: 她覺得累，就早早睡了。
examples.en: Feeling tired, she went to bed early.

examples.text: Having finished his homework, Tom went out to play.
examples.zh: 湯姆寫完功課後就出去玩了。
examples.en: Having finished his homework, Tom went out to play.

examples.text: Surrounded by mountains, the village is very quiet.
examples.zh: 那個村子四面環山，非常安靜。
examples.en: Surrounded by mountains, the village is very quiet.

quiz.q: （　）the news, she started to cry.
quiz.zh: 聽到那個消息，她開始哭了。
quiz.en: Hearing the news, she started to cry.

quiz.q: （　）by many tourists, the temple is always crowded.
quiz.zh: 這座廟有很多遊客造訪，總是很擁擠。
quiz.en: Visited by many tourists, the temple is always crowded.

quiz.q: （　）the report, I sent it to my boss.
quiz.zh: 寫完報告後，我把它寄給老闆。
quiz.en: Having written the report, I sent it to my boss.

title.zh: 分詞形容詞：interesting 和 interested

form.zh: -ing：讓人有某種感覺的人事物（boring 令人無聊的）・-ed：人自己的感覺（bored 覺得無聊）
form.en: -ing: what causes the feeling (boring) · -ed: how the person feels (bored)

explain.zh: -ing 形容詞描述「讓人覺得…的東西」，-ed 描述「人感到…」：The movie was boring, so I was bored.（電影很無聊，所以我覺得無聊。）I'm interested in history because it's interesting.
explain.en: -ing adjectives describe what causes a feeling; -ed adjectives describe how people feel: The movie was boring, so I was bored. I'm interested in history because it's interesting.

notes.zh: 常見的一組：exciting／excited、tiring／tired、surprising／surprised、confusing／confused。
notes.en: Common pairs: exciting / excited, tiring / tired, surprising / surprised, confusing / confused.

mistakes.wrong: I'm very boring in math class.
mistakes.right: I'm very bored in math class.
mistakes.zh: 說自己的感覺用 bored（I'm boring 是「我很無趣」）。
mistakes.en: Your feeling is bored (I'm boring means you're dull).

mistakes.wrong: The news was very surprised.
mistakes.right: The news was very surprising.
mistakes.zh: 讓人驚訝的消息用 surprising。
mistakes.en: News that surprises is surprising.

examples.text: The trip was tiring, but we were very excited.
examples.zh: 旅程很累，但我們很興奮。
examples.en: The trip was tiring, but we were very excited.

examples.text: I was confused by the confusing instructions.
examples.zh: 說明寫得很混亂，讓我看得一頭霧水。
examples.en: I was confused by the confusing instructions.

examples.text: Are you interested in joining the club?
examples.zh: 你有興趣加入社團嗎？
examples.en: Are you interested in joining the club?

quiz.q: The ending of the story was really（　）.
quiz.zh: 故事的結局真的很令人驚訝。
quiz.en: The ending of the story was really surprising.

quiz.q: After the long hike, we were all（　）.
quiz.zh: 長途健行後，我們都累壞了。
quiz.en: After the long hike, we were all exhausted.

quiz.q: It's（　）to hear that you got the job!
quiz.zh: 聽到你得到那份工作真令人興奮！
quiz.en: It's exciting to hear that you got the job!

form.zh: make／let／have ＋ 受詞 ＋ 原形・get ＋ 受詞 ＋ to V・have／get ＋ 東西 ＋ p.p.（請人把東西…）
form.en: make / let / have + object + verb · get + object + to verb · have / get + thing + p.p. (have something done)

explain.zh: make 是「迫使」，let 是「讓、允許」，have 是「叫（某人做）」，後面都接原形：My mom made me clean my room. Let me help you. 請別人幫你處理東西用 have ＋ 東西 ＋ p.p.：I had my hair cut.（我去剪了頭髮。）
explain.en: make means force, let means allow, have means arrange for someone to do it — all with the bare verb: My mom made me clean my room. Let me help you. For services: have + thing + p.p.: I had my hair cut.

notes.zh: 被動時 make 要加 to：I was made to wait.
notes.en: In the passive, make takes to: I was made to wait.

mistakes.wrong: My boss made me to work late.
mistakes.right: My boss made me work late.
mistakes.zh: make 後面接原形。
mistakes.en: make takes the bare verb.

mistakes.wrong: I cut my hair at the salon yesterday.
mistakes.right: I had my hair cut at the salon yesterday.
mistakes.zh: 請別人剪頭髮用 have ＋ hair ＋ cut。
mistakes.en: Someone else cut it: have my hair cut.

examples.text: The sad movie made everyone cry.
examples.zh: 那部悲傷的電影讓大家都哭了。
examples.en: The sad movie made everyone cry.

examples.text: My parents let me stay up late on Fridays.
examples.zh: 我爸媽星期五讓我晚睡。
examples.en: My parents let me stay up late on Fridays.

examples.text: We're having our kitchen repainted.
examples.zh: 我們請人重新粉刷廚房。
examples.en: We're having our kitchen repainted.

quiz.q: The teacher let us（　）early.
quiz.zh: 老師讓我們早點走。
quiz.en: The teacher let us leave early.

quiz.q: I need to get my phone（　）.
quiz.zh: 我得把手機送修。
quiz.en: I need to get my phone repaired.

quiz.q: I finally got my brother（　）me his bike.
quiz.zh: 我終於說服哥哥把腳踏車借我了。
quiz.en: I finally got my brother to lend me his bike.

form.zh: see／hear／watch／feel ＋ 受詞 ＋ 原形（看到整個過程）／V-ing（看到正在進行）
form.en: see / hear / watch / feel + object + verb (the whole action) / verb-ing (part of it, in progress)

explain.zh: 感官動詞後面的動作可以用原形或 V-ing：I saw him cross the street.（看到他過完馬路，整個過程）I saw him crossing the street.（看到他正在過馬路）兩種都對，意思略有不同。
explain.en: After perception verbs the action can be a bare verb or -ing: I saw him cross the street (the whole action), I saw him crossing the street (in progress). Both are correct with slightly different meanings.

notes.zh: 被動時原形要加 to：He was seen to enter the building.
notes.en: In the passive the bare verb takes to: He was seen to enter the building.

mistakes.wrong: I heard someone to call my name.
mistakes.right: I heard someone call my name.
mistakes.zh: 感官動詞後面不加 to。
mistakes.en: No to after a perception verb.

mistakes.wrong: We watched the sun to set.
mistakes.right: We watched the sun set.
mistakes.zh: watch 後面接原形或 V-ing。
mistakes.en: watch takes the bare verb or -ing.

examples.text: I heard the baby crying in the next room.
examples.zh: 我聽到寶寶在隔壁房間哭。
examples.en: I heard the baby crying in the next room.

examples.text: Did you see anyone leave the building?
examples.zh: 你有看到任何人離開大樓嗎？
examples.en: Did you see anyone leave the building?

examples.text: She felt the ground shake during the earthquake.
examples.zh: 地震時她感覺到地面在搖。
examples.en: She felt the ground shake during the earthquake.

quiz.q: I saw a cat（　）up the tree.
quiz.zh: 我看到一隻貓爬上樹。
quiz.en: I saw a cat climb up the tree.

quiz.q: Can you hear the birds（　）?
quiz.zh: 你聽得到鳥在唱歌嗎？
quiz.en: Can you hear the birds singing?

quiz.q: He was seen（　）the store at midnight.
quiz.zh: 有人看到他半夜進了那家店。
quiz.en: He was seen to enter the store at midnight.

form.zh: that ＋ 完整子句（…這件事）・what ＋ 缺東西的子句（…的東西）・whether／if ＋ 子句（是否）
form.en: that + complete clause · what + clause missing something (the thing that) · whether / if + clause

explain.zh: 一個子句可以當名詞用：That he lied surprised me.（他說謊這件事讓我驚訝。）What you said is true.（你說的是真的。）I don't know whether he'll come. what 等於 the thing that，後面的子句少一個受詞或主詞。
explain.en: A clause can work as a noun: That he lied surprised me. What you said is true. I don't know whether he'll come. what = the thing that, and its clause is missing an object or subject.

notes.zh: 主詞是 that 子句時，常改成 It ... that：It surprised me that he lied.
notes.en: A that clause subject is often moved: It surprised me that he lied.

mistakes.wrong: That you need is a good rest.
mistakes.right: What you need is a good rest.
mistakes.zh: need 缺受詞，用 what。
mistakes.en: need lacks an object: what.

mistakes.wrong: I can't believe what she won the contest.
mistakes.right: I can't believe that she won the contest.
mistakes.zh: 子句完整，用 that。
mistakes.en: The clause is complete: that.

examples.text: What I really want is a long vacation.
examples.zh: 我真正想要的是一個長假。
examples.en: What I really want is a long vacation.

examples.text: The problem is that we don't have enough time.
examples.zh: 問題是我們時間不夠。
examples.en: The problem is that we don't have enough time.

examples.text: Whether we go or not depends on the weather.
examples.zh: 要不要去要看天氣。
examples.en: Whether we go or not depends on the weather.

quiz.q: （　）she said made everyone laugh.
quiz.zh: 她說的話讓大家都笑了。
quiz.en: What she said made everyone laugh.

quiz.q: The truth is（　）I forgot your birthday.
quiz.zh: 事實是我忘了你的生日。
quiz.en: The truth is that I forgot your birthday.

quiz.q: I'm not sure（　）the store is open today.
quiz.zh: 我不確定那家店今天有沒有開。
quiz.en: I'm not sure whether the store is open today.

form.zh: It is／was ＋ 要強調的部分 ＋ that ＋ 句子其他部分
form.en: It is / was + the part to stress + that + the rest

explain.zh: 想強調句子的某一部分，把它放在 It is／was 和 that 之間：Tom broke the window. → It was Tom that broke the window.（打破窗戶的是湯姆。）It was yesterday that I saw her.
explain.en: To stress one part of a sentence, put it between It is / was and that: It was Tom that broke the window. It was yesterday that I saw her.

notes.zh: 強調人時也可以用 who：It was Tom who broke the window.
notes.en: For people who also works: It was Tom who broke the window.

notes.zh: It was not until … that …：直到…才…：It was not until midnight that he came home.
notes.en: It was not until … that …: It was not until midnight that he came home.

mistakes.wrong: It was in Paris where I met her.
mistakes.right: It was in Paris that I met her.
mistakes.zh: 強調句固定用 that。
mistakes.en: Cleft sentences use that.

mistakes.wrong: It is my parents that supports me.
mistakes.right: It is my parents that support me.
mistakes.zh: 動詞跟著被強調的 parents 用複數。
mistakes.en: The verb agrees with parents.

examples.text: It was my grandmother who taught me to cook.
examples.zh: 教我做菜的是我奶奶。
examples.en: It was my grandmother who taught me to cook.

examples.text: It is hard work that leads to success.
examples.zh: 帶來成功的是努力。
examples.en: It is hard work that leads to success.

examples.text: It was not until I got home that I noticed my phone was gone.
examples.zh: 直到回到家，我才發現手機不見了。
examples.en: It was not until I got home that I noticed my phone was gone.

quiz.q: It was at the night market（　）I lost my wallet.
quiz.zh: 我是在夜市弄丟錢包的。
quiz.en: It was at the night market that I lost my wallet.

quiz.q: It was not until ten o'clock（　）the meeting ended.
quiz.zh: 會議直到十點才結束。
quiz.en: It was not until ten o'clock that the meeting ended.

quiz.q: （　）was Edison who invented the light bulb.
quiz.zh: 發明電燈泡的是愛迪生。
quiz.en: It was Edison who invented the light bulb.

points.pattern: too … to・enough to・so … that・such … that

title.en: too … to, enough to, so … that, such … that

form.zh: too ＋ 形 ＋ to V（太…不能）・形 ＋ enough to V（夠…可以）・so ＋ 形 ／ such (a) ＋ 形 ＋ 名 ＋ that（如此…以致）
form.en: too + adj + to verb · adj + enough to verb · so + adj / such (a) + adj + noun + that

explain.zh: 說程度和結果：The box is too heavy to lift.（箱子太重搬不動。）She is old enough to drive.（她夠大可以開車了。）It was so hot that we stayed inside. It was such a hot day that we stayed inside.
explain.en: For degree and result: The box is too heavy to lift. She is old enough to drive. It was so hot that we stayed inside. It was such a hot day that we stayed inside.

notes.zh: enough 放在形容詞後面，名詞前面：tall enough、enough money。
notes.en: enough goes after adjectives but before nouns: tall enough, enough money.

mistakes.wrong: He is enough tall to reach the shelf.
mistakes.right: He is tall enough to reach the shelf.
mistakes.zh: enough 放在形容詞後面。
mistakes.en: enough follows the adjective.

mistakes.wrong: It was so a good movie that I saw it twice.
mistakes.right: It was such a good movie that I saw it twice.
mistakes.zh: 後面有名詞用 such a。
mistakes.en: With a noun use such a.

examples.text: The tea is too hot to drink.
examples.zh: 茶太燙了，不能喝。
examples.en: The tea is too hot to drink.

examples.text: He was so tired that he fell asleep on the bus.
examples.zh: 他累到在公車上睡著了。
examples.en: He was so tired that he fell asleep on the bus.

examples.text: We don't have enough chairs for everyone.
examples.zh: 椅子不夠大家坐。
examples.en: We don't have enough chairs for everyone.

quiz.q: This shirt is（　）small for me to wear.
quiz.zh: 這件襯衫太小了，我穿不下。
quiz.en: This shirt is too small for me to wear.

quiz.q: It was（　）a boring lecture that half the class fell asleep.
quiz.zh: 那場演講太無聊了，半個班都睡著了。
quiz.en: It was such a boring lecture that half the class fell asleep.

quiz.q: Is the water warm（　）to swim in?
quiz.zh: 水夠溫暖可以游泳嗎？
quiz.en: Is the water warm enough to swim in?

points.pattern: Never have I …・Not only … but also

form.zh: 否定詞放句首 ＋ 助動詞 ＋ 主詞 ＋ 動詞：Never／Rarely／Seldom／Not only／Only then／No sooner … than
form.en: negative word first + auxiliary + subject + verb: Never / Rarely / Seldom / Not only / Only then / No sooner … than

explain.zh: 否定或限定的字放在句首加強語氣時，後面要像問句一樣倒裝：I have never seen such a view. → Never have I seen such a view.（我從沒看過這麼美的景色。）Not only is she smart, but she is also kind.
explain.en: When a negative or limiting word starts the sentence for emphasis, the rest is inverted like a question: Never have I seen such a view. Not only is she smart, but she is also kind.

notes.zh: 一般動詞要補 do／does／did：Seldom does he eat breakfast.
notes.en: Ordinary verbs need do / does / did: Seldom does he eat breakfast.

mistakes.wrong: Never I have eaten such good food.
mistakes.right: Never have I eaten such good food.
mistakes.zh: Never 在句首要倒裝。
mistakes.en: Never at the start needs inversion.

mistakes.wrong: Rarely he goes to the movies.
mistakes.right: Rarely does he go to the movies.
mistakes.zh: 一般動詞倒裝要加 does，動詞回原形。
mistakes.en: Ordinary verbs need does + bare verb.

examples.text: Not only did he forget my birthday, but he also forgot our dinner.
examples.zh: 他不但忘了我的生日，連我們的晚餐約會也忘了。
examples.en: Not only did he forget my birthday, but he also forgot our dinner.

examples.text: Seldom do we see such kindness.
examples.zh: 我們很少看到這樣的善意。
examples.en: Seldom do we see such kindness.

examples.text: Only then did I understand what she meant.
examples.zh: 直到那時我才明白她的意思。
examples.en: Only then did I understand what she meant.

quiz.q: Never（　）such a beautiful sunset.
quiz.zh: 我從沒看過這麼美的夕陽。
quiz.en: Never have I seen such a beautiful sunset.

quiz.q: Not only（　）fluent English, but she also speaks Spanish.
quiz.zh: 她不但英文流利，還會說西班牙文。
quiz.en: Not only does she speak fluent English, but she also speaks Spanish.

quiz.q: Rarely（　）late for work.
quiz.zh: 他很少上班遲到。
quiz.en: Rarely is he late for work.

title.zh: 助動詞 ＋ have ＋ p.p.：對過去的推測和後悔

form.zh: must have p.p.（當時一定…）・can't have p.p.（當時不可能…）・should have p.p.（當時應該…卻沒有）・could／might have p.p.（當時可能…）
form.en: must have p.p. (surely did) · can't have p.p. (surely didn't) · should have p.p. (ought to have, but didn't) · could / might have p.p. (possibly did)

explain.zh: 對過去的事推測或後悔：The ground is wet. It must have rained.（地是濕的，一定下過雨。）I should have brought a jacket.（我早該帶外套的。）He might have missed the bus.
explain.en: For guesses and regrets about the past: The ground is wet. It must have rained. I should have brought a jacket. He might have missed the bus.

notes.zh: shouldn't have p.p. 是「當時不該…卻做了」：You shouldn't have said that.
notes.en: shouldn't have p.p. means you did it but shouldn't have: You shouldn't have said that.

mistakes.wrong: She must has left already.
mistakes.right: She must have left already.
mistakes.zh: 助動詞後面一律用 have。
mistakes.en: After a modal it's always have.

mistakes.wrong: I should studied harder.
mistakes.right: I should have studied harder.
mistakes.zh: 後悔過去的事用 should have ＋ p.p.。
mistakes.en: Past regret: should have + p.p.

examples.text: You must have been tired after the long flight.
examples.zh: 長途飛行後你一定很累吧。
examples.en: You must have been tired after the long flight.

examples.text: We should have booked the tickets earlier.
examples.zh: 我們應該早點訂票的。
examples.en: We should have booked the tickets earlier.

examples.text: He can't have finished already — he only started an hour ago.
examples.zh: 他不可能已經做完了，他一小時前才開始。
examples.en: He can't have finished already — he only started an hour ago.

quiz.q: The lights are off. They（　）gone to bed.
quiz.zh: 燈都關了，他們一定已經睡了。
quiz.en: The lights are off. They must have gone to bed.

quiz.q: I failed the test. I（　）more.
quiz.zh: 我考試不及格，早該多讀一點的。
quiz.en: I failed the test. I should have studied more.

quiz.q: She（　）seen me. She was in Japan at the time.
quiz.zh: 她不可能看到我，她那時在日本。
quiz.en: She can't have seen me. She was in Japan at the time.

points.pattern: used to V・be used to V-ing

title.zh: used to 和 be used to
title.en: used to and be used to

form.zh: used to ＋ 原形（以前常常…，現在不了）・be／get used to ＋ V-ing／名詞（習慣於…）
form.en: used to + verb (did in the past, not now) · be / get used to + verb-ing / noun (be accustomed to)

explain.zh: used to ＋ 原形說過去的習慣或狀態：I used to live in Kaohsiung.（我以前住在高雄。）be used to ＋ V-ing 是「已經習慣」：I'm used to getting up early.（我習慣早起了。）get used to 是「漸漸習慣」。
explain.en: used to + verb is a past habit or state: I used to live in Kaohsiung. be used to + -ing means “be accustomed to”: I'm used to getting up early. get used to means “become accustomed”.

notes.zh: be used to 的 to 是介系詞，後面接 V-ing 或名詞。
notes.en: In be used to, to is a preposition: -ing or a noun follows.

notes.zh: 否定和疑問：didn't use to、Did you use to …?
notes.en: Negatives and questions: didn't use to, Did you use to …?

mistakes.wrong: I'm used to drive on the left.
mistakes.right: I'm used to driving on the left.
mistakes.zh: be used to 後面接 V-ing。
mistakes.en: be used to takes -ing.

mistakes.wrong: She use to play the piano.
mistakes.right: She used to play the piano.
mistakes.zh: 肯定句寫成 used to。
mistakes.en: In statements it's used to.

examples.text: There used to be a cinema on this street.
examples.zh: 這條街以前有一間電影院。
examples.en: There used to be a cinema on this street.

examples.text: It took me months to get used to the cold weather.
examples.zh: 我花了好幾個月才習慣寒冷的天氣。
examples.en: It took me months to get used to the cold weather.

examples.text: Did you use to have long hair?
examples.zh: 你以前是長頭髮嗎？
examples.en: Did you use to have long hair?

quiz.q: My dad used to（　）a lot, but he quit.
quiz.zh: 我爸爸以前很常抽菸，但戒了。
quiz.en: My dad used to smoke a lot, but he quit.

quiz.q: I'm not used to（　）spicy food.
quiz.zh: 我不習慣吃辣。
quiz.en: I'm not used to eating spicy food.

quiz.q: You'll soon get used to（　）in a big city.
quiz.zh: 你很快就會習慣住在大城市。
quiz.en: You'll soon get used to living in a big city.

title.en: Contrast: although, despite, in spite of

form.zh: although／though／even though ＋ 子句・despite／in spite of ＋ 名詞／V-ing
form.en: although / though / even though + clause · despite / in spite of + noun / verb-ing

explain.zh: although 後面接完整的句子：Although it was raining, we went out. despite／in spite of 後面接名詞或 V-ing：Despite the rain, we went out. In spite of feeling sick, she went to school.
explain.en: although takes a full clause: Although it was raining, we went out. despite / in spite of take a noun or -ing: Despite the rain, we went out. In spite of feeling sick, she went to school.

notes.zh: despite 後面沒有 of；in spite of 要有 of。
notes.en: despite has no of; in spite of does.

notes.zh: although 和 but 不一起用。
notes.en: Don't use although and but together.

mistakes.wrong: Despite it was late, he kept working.
mistakes.right: Although it was late, he kept working.
mistakes.zh: 後面是完整句子要用 although。
mistakes.en: A full clause needs although.

mistakes.wrong: Despite of the traffic, we arrived on time.
mistakes.right: Despite the traffic, we arrived on time.
mistakes.zh: despite 不加 of。
mistakes.en: despite has no of.

examples.text: Even though he's rich, he lives a simple life.
examples.zh: 他雖然有錢，卻過著簡樸的生活。
examples.en: Even though he's rich, he lives a simple life.

examples.text: Despite the high price, the tickets sold out quickly.
examples.zh: 儘管票價很高，票還是很快就賣完了。
examples.en: Despite the high price, the tickets sold out quickly.

examples.text: In spite of being tired, she finished the race.
examples.zh: 儘管很累，她還是跑完了全程。
examples.en: In spite of being tired, she finished the race.

quiz.q: （　）the bad weather, the concert went on.
quiz.zh: 儘管天氣不好，演唱會照常舉行。
quiz.en: Despite the bad weather, the concert went on.

quiz.q: （　）she studied hard, she didn't pass.
quiz.zh: 雖然她很用功，還是沒通過。
quiz.en: Although she studied hard, she didn't pass.

quiz.q: He went to work in spite of（　）a cold.
quiz.zh: 他雖然感冒了，還是去上班。
quiz.en: He went to work in spite of having a cold.

title.en: Purpose: so that, in order to

form.zh: in order to／so as to ＋ 原形・so that ＋ 子句（常有 can／could／will／would）
form.en: in order to / so as to + verb · so that + clause (often with can / could / will / would)

explain.zh: 說「為了…」：She got up early in order to catch the first train. 主詞不同或要用助動詞時用 so that：I'll speak slowly so that everyone can understand.（我會說慢一點，好讓大家都聽得懂。）
explain.en: For purpose: She got up early in order to catch the first train. With a different subject or a modal, use so that: I'll speak slowly so that everyone can understand.

notes.zh: 否定目的：in order not to ＋ 原形、so that … won't／wouldn't。
notes.en: Negative purpose: in order not to + verb, so that … won't / wouldn't.

mistakes.wrong: I saved money in order buying a laptop.
mistakes.right: I saved money in order to buy a laptop.
mistakes.zh: in order to 後面接原形。
mistakes.en: in order to takes the bare verb.

mistakes.wrong: Turn off the light so that the baby sleeps can.
mistakes.right: Turn off the light so that the baby can sleep.
mistakes.zh: so that 後面是正常語序的子句。
mistakes.en: so that takes a normal clause.

examples.text: He wrote it down so that he wouldn't forget.
examples.zh: 他把它寫下來，免得忘記。
examples.en: He wrote it down so that he wouldn't forget.

examples.text: We left early in order to avoid the traffic.
examples.zh: 我們早點出發，為了避開車潮。
examples.en: We left early in order to avoid the traffic.

examples.text: Speak louder so that the people at the back can hear.
examples.zh: 說大聲一點，讓後面的人也聽得到。
examples.en: Speak louder so that the people at the back can hear.

quiz.q: She whispered（　）not to wake the baby.
quiz.zh: 她小聲說話，以免吵醒寶寶。
quiz.en: She whispered in order not to wake the baby.

quiz.q: I'll send you the map so that you（　）find the place.
quiz.zh: 我會把地圖傳給你，讓你找得到地方。
quiz.en: I'll send you the map so that you can find the place.

quiz.q: He works two jobs in order to（　）his family.
quiz.zh: 他做兩份工作來養家。
quiz.en: He works two jobs in order to support his family.

form.zh: said／told sb ＋ (that) ＋ 子句：時態往過去退一步（is → was、will → would、did → had done）・asked ＋ if／wh- ＋ 直述句語序・told／asked sb ＋ (not) to V
form.en: said / told sb + (that) + clause: tenses move back (is → was, will → would, did → had done) · asked + if / wh- + statement order · told / asked sb + (not) to verb

explain.zh: 轉述別人說過的話時，時態通常往過去退一步，代名詞也要換："I'm tired," she said. → She said (that) she was tired. 轉述問句用直述句語序：He asked me where I lived. 轉述命令用 told ＋ 人 ＋ to V。
explain.en: When reporting, tenses usually move back and pronouns change: She said (that) she was tired. Reported questions use statement order: He asked me where I lived. Reported orders: told + person + to verb.

notes.zh: say 後面不直接接人，tell 後面要接人：said that … ／ told me that …
notes.en: say doesn't take a person directly; tell does: said that … / told me that …

notes.zh: 時間地點也會變：tomorrow → the next day、here → there。
notes.en: Time and place words change too: tomorrow → the next day, here → there.

mistakes.wrong: She said me that she was busy.
mistakes.right: She told me that she was busy.
mistakes.zh: 說給某人聽用 told me。
mistakes.en: With a person, use told me.

mistakes.wrong: He asked me where did I live.
mistakes.right: He asked me where I lived.
mistakes.zh: 轉述問句用直述句語序。
mistakes.en: Reported questions use statement order.

examples.text: He said he would call me later.
examples.zh: 他說他晚點會打給我。
examples.en: He said he would call me later.

examples.text: The teacher told us not to use our phones.
examples.zh: 老師叫我們不要用手機。
examples.en: The teacher told us not to use our phones.

examples.text: She asked me if I had finished the report.
examples.zh: 她問我報告寫完了沒。
examples.en: She asked me if I had finished the report.

quiz.q: "I'm hungry," said Tim. → Tim said that he（　）hungry.
quiz.zh: 提姆說他餓了。
quiz.en: Tim said that he was hungry.

quiz.q: My mom（　）me to clean my room.
quiz.zh: 我媽媽叫我打掃房間。
quiz.en: My mom told me to clean my room.

quiz.q: She asked me what time（　）.
quiz.zh: 她問我現在幾點。
quiz.en: She asked me what time it was.

title.zh: 接 to V 和 V-ing 意思不同的動詞
title.en: Verbs with different meanings with to-verb and -ing

form.zh: stop V-ing（停止做）／stop to V（停下來去做）・remember／forget V-ing（記得／忘了做過）／to V（記得／忘了要做）・try V-ing（試試看做）／try to V（努力設法做）
form.en: stop -ing (quit) / stop to (pause in order to) · remember / forget -ing (the past) / to (a task) · try -ing (experiment) / try to (make an effort)

explain.zh: 有些動詞接 to V 和 V-ing 意思不一樣：He stopped smoking.（他戒菸了。）He stopped to smoke.（他停下來抽根菸。）Remember to lock the door.（記得鎖門。）I remember locking the door.（我記得我鎖過門。）
explain.en: Some verbs change meaning: He stopped smoking (quit) / He stopped to smoke (paused to smoke). Remember to lock the door (don't forget) / I remember locking the door (I did it).

notes.zh: regret V-ing 是「後悔做過」，regret to V 是「很遺憾要（告知）」：We regret to inform you …
notes.en: regret -ing = be sorry you did; regret to = be sorry to (say): We regret to inform you …

mistakes.wrong: Don't forget sending me the photos.
mistakes.right: Don't forget to send me the photos.
mistakes.zh: 「別忘了要做」用 to V。
mistakes.en: A task you mustn't forget: to verb.

mistakes.wrong: I'll never forget to see the ocean for the first time.
mistakes.right: I'll never forget seeing the ocean for the first time.
mistakes.zh: 忘不了「做過的事」用 V-ing。
mistakes.en: A memory of something done: -ing.

examples.text: We stopped to buy some drinks on the way.
examples.zh: 我們半路停下來買飲料。
examples.en: We stopped to buy some drinks on the way.

examples.text: If your computer is slow, try restarting it.
examples.zh: 電腦很慢的話，試試看重新開機。
examples.en: If your computer is slow, try restarting it.

examples.text: I remember meeting her at a concert.
examples.zh: 我記得在一場演唱會上見過她。
examples.en: I remember meeting her at a concert.

quiz.q: Please stop（　）. I'm trying to sleep.
quiz.zh: 請別再講話了，我想睡覺。
quiz.en: Please stop talking. I'm trying to sleep.

quiz.q: Remember（　）the plants while I'm away.
quiz.zh: 我不在時記得要澆花。
quiz.en: Remember to water the plants while I'm away.

quiz.q: I'll never forget（　）the top of Yushan.
quiz.zh: 我永遠忘不了登上玉山頂的那一刻。
quiz.en: I'll never forget reaching the top of Yushan.

points.pattern: The ＋ 比較級, the ＋ 比較級

form.zh: The ＋ 比較級 ＋ 主詞 ＋ 動詞, the ＋ 比較級 ＋ 主詞 ＋ 動詞
form.en: The + comparative + subject + verb, the + comparative + subject + verb

explain.zh: 說兩件事一起變化：The more you practice, the better you get.（你練得越多，就會越好。）The sooner, the better.（越快越好。）比較級放在 the 後面，句首要有 the。
explain.en: For two things that change together: The more you practice, the better you get. The sooner, the better. Each half starts with the + comparative.

notes.zh: 名詞也可以：The more money he makes, the more he spends.
notes.en: Nouns work too: The more money he makes, the more he spends.

mistakes.wrong: More you read, more you learn.
mistakes.right: The more you read, the more you learn.
mistakes.zh: 兩邊都要有 the。
mistakes.en: Both halves need the.

mistakes.wrong: The harder you work, the more successful you will be more.
mistakes.right: The harder you work, the more successful you will be.
mistakes.zh: 比較級只放在 the 後面一次。
mistakes.en: The comparative appears once, after the.

examples.text: The older I get, the more I appreciate my parents.
examples.zh: 我年紀越大，越感謝我的爸媽。
examples.en: The older I get, the more I appreciate my parents.

examples.text: The earlier we leave, the less traffic there will be.
examples.zh: 我們越早出發，車就越少。
examples.en: The earlier we leave, the less traffic there will be.

examples.text: The more, the merrier!
examples.zh: 人越多越熱鬧！
examples.en: The more, the merrier!

quiz.q: The more you exercise, the（　）you will feel.
quiz.zh: 你運動越多，就會覺得越健康。
quiz.en: The more you exercise, the healthier you will feel.

quiz.q: （　）hotter it gets, the more water you should drink.
quiz.zh: 天氣越熱，你就應該喝越多水。
quiz.en: The hotter it gets, the more water you should drink.

quiz.q: The（　）I think about it, the less I like the idea.
quiz.zh: 我越想，就越不喜歡這個點子。
quiz.en: The more I think about it, the less I like the idea.

form.zh: ask／tell／want／expect／allow／encourage／remind／advise ＋ 受詞 ＋ (not) to ＋ 原形
form.en: ask / tell / want / expect / allow / encourage / remind / advise + object + (not) to + verb

explain.zh: 這些動詞後面先接「人」，再接 to ＋ 原形，表示要那個人做的事：My parents want me to be a doctor.（我爸媽希望我當醫生。）The doctor advised him to rest.
explain.en: These verbs take a person, then to + verb for what that person should do: My parents want me to be a doctor. The doctor advised him to rest.

notes.zh: 否定放在 to 前面：She reminded me not to be late.
notes.en: The negative goes before to: She reminded me not to be late.

notes.zh: suggest 不能用這個句型：I suggest that he (should) rest.
notes.en: suggest doesn't fit this pattern: I suggest that he (should) rest.

mistakes.wrong: I want that you come to my party.
mistakes.right: I want you to come to my party.
mistakes.zh: want ＋ 人 ＋ to V。
mistakes.en: want + person + to verb.

mistakes.wrong: She told me don't worry.
mistakes.right: She told me not to worry.
mistakes.zh: 否定是 not to ＋ 原形。
mistakes.en: The negative is not to + verb.

examples.text: The coach encouraged us to keep trying.
examples.zh: 教練鼓勵我們繼續努力。
examples.en: The coach encouraged us to keep trying.

examples.text: Could you remind me to buy milk?
examples.zh: 你可以提醒我買牛奶嗎？
examples.en: Could you remind me to buy milk?

examples.text: My school doesn't allow students to dye their hair.
examples.zh: 我們學校不准學生染頭髮。
examples.en: My school doesn't allow students to dye their hair.

quiz.q: The teacher asked us（　）quiet.
quiz.zh: 老師要我們保持安靜。
quiz.en: The teacher asked us to be quiet.

quiz.q: My dad told me（　）stay out too late.
quiz.zh: 我爸爸叫我不要在外面待太晚。
quiz.en: My dad told me not to stay out too late.

quiz.q: I'd like（　）join us for dinner.
quiz.zh: 我想請你跟我們一起吃晚餐。
quiz.en: I'd like you to join us for dinner.

form.zh: It takes ＋ 人 ＋ 時間 ＋ to V・人 ＋ spend ＋ 時間／錢 ＋ V-ing／on ＋ 名詞・東西 ＋ cost ＋ 人 ＋ 錢
form.en: It takes + person + time + to verb · person + spend + time / money + verb-ing / on + noun · thing + cost + person + money

explain.zh: 三種說「花」的句型主詞不同：It takes me an hour to get to work.（我通勤要一小時。）I spend an hour commuting every day. This bag cost me 2,000 dollars.（這個包包花了我兩千元。）
explain.en: Three ways to say “spend”, each with a different subject: It takes me an hour to get to work. I spend an hour commuting every day. This bag cost me 2,000 dollars.

notes.zh: spend 後面接 V-ing 或 on ＋ 名詞，不接 to V。
notes.en: spend takes -ing or on + noun, never to + verb.

mistakes.wrong: I spent two hours to finish the puzzle.
mistakes.right: I spent two hours finishing the puzzle.
mistakes.zh: spend 時間 ＋ V-ing。
mistakes.en: spend time + -ing.

mistakes.wrong: It took me to clean the house three hours.
mistakes.right: It took me three hours to clean the house.
mistakes.zh: 順序是 It takes ＋ 人 ＋ 時間 ＋ to V。
mistakes.en: Order: It takes + person + time + to verb.

examples.text: How long does it take to walk to the station?
examples.zh: 走到車站要多久？
examples.en: How long does it take to walk to the station?

examples.text: She spends too much money on clothes.
examples.zh: 她花太多錢買衣服。
examples.en: She spends too much money on clothes.

examples.text: The repairs cost us a fortune.
examples.zh: 修理花了我們一大筆錢。
examples.en: The repairs cost us a fortune.

quiz.q: It（　）me two days to read this novel.
quiz.zh: 我花了兩天讀完這本小說。
quiz.en: It took me two days to read this novel.

quiz.q: He spends hours（　）video games every weekend.
quiz.zh: 他每個週末都花好幾個小時打電動。
quiz.en: He spends hours playing video games every weekend.

quiz.q: How much did your new phone（　）?
quiz.zh: 你的新手機花了多少錢？
quiz.en: How much did your new phone cost?

form.zh: 主詞 ＋ 否定 ＋ 動詞 ＋ until ＋ 時間／子句・Not until ＋ 時間／子句 ＋ 助動詞 ＋ 主詞 ＋ 動詞（倒裝）
form.en: subject + negative verb + until + time / clause · Not until + time / clause + auxiliary + subject + verb (inverted)

explain.zh: 英文說「直到…才…」要用否定：I didn't go to bed until midnight.（我直到半夜才睡。）Not until 放句首時，主句要倒裝：Not until midnight did I go to bed.
explain.en: English says “didn't … until”: I didn't go to bed until midnight. With Not until at the front, invert the main clause: Not until midnight did I go to bed.

notes.zh: 也可以說 It was not until midnight that I went to bed.（強調句）
notes.en: Also: It was not until midnight that I went to bed (a cleft).

mistakes.wrong: I went to bed until midnight.
mistakes.right: I didn't go to bed until midnight.
mistakes.zh: 「直到…才」要用否定 didn't … until。
mistakes.en: “Not until” needs didn't … until.

mistakes.wrong: Not until he left I noticed the gift.
mistakes.right: Not until he left did I notice the gift.
mistakes.zh: Not until 在句首，主句要倒裝。
mistakes.en: Not until at the front needs inversion.

examples.text: She didn't start learning English until she was twenty.
examples.zh: 她直到二十歲才開始學英文。
examples.en: She didn't start learning English until she was twenty.

examples.text: Not until I lost it did I realize how much I loved it.
examples.zh: 直到失去了，我才發現自己有多喜歡它。
examples.en: Not until I lost it did I realize how much I loved it.

examples.text: The store won't open until ten.
examples.zh: 那家店要到十點才開。
examples.en: The store won't open until ten.

quiz.q: He（　）home until after midnight.
quiz.zh: 他直到半夜過後才回家。
quiz.en: He didn't come home until after midnight.

quiz.q: Not until the end of the movie（　）who the killer was.
quiz.zh: 直到電影結尾，我才知道兇手是誰。
quiz.en: Not until the end of the movie did I know who the killer was.

quiz.q: We can't start（　）everyone arrives.
quiz.zh: 要等大家都到了，我們才能開始。
quiz.en: We can't start until everyone arrives.
